router-bound:
#!/bin/sh
# managed-by: multi-codex router
# Generated by multi-codex from directory bindings. Do not edit; use `multi-codex bind` / `unbind`.
here=$(/bin/pwd -P 2>/dev/null || pwd -P) || exit 1
best=0
target=''
stale=''
if [ 1 -gt "$best" ]; then best=1; target=/home/u/.local/bin/codex-home; stale=''; fi
case "$here/" in
  /home/u/gone/*)
    if [ 12 -gt "$best" ]; then best=12; target=''; stale='account ghost bound to /home/u/gone is not registered; run: multi-codex unbind /home/u/gone'; fi ;;
esac
case "$here/" in
  /home/u/src/*)
    if [ 11 -gt "$best" ]; then best=11; target=/home/u/.local/bin/codex-work; stale=''; fi ;;
esac
case "$here/" in
  '/home/u/src/it'"'"'s dir'/*)
    if [ 20 -gt "$best" ]; then best=20; target=/home/u/.local/bin/codex-home; stale=''; fi ;;
esac
if [ -n "$stale" ]; then
  printf 'multi-codex: %s\n' "$stale" >&2
  exit 1
fi
if [ -n "$target" ]; then
  if [ ! -x "$target" ]; then
    printf 'multi-codex: launcher %s is missing; run multi-codex apply\n' "$target" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  exec "$target" "$@"
fi
printf 'multi-codex: no account is bound to %s or its parents; running codex (the default account)\n' "$here" >&2
if ! command -v codex >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "multi-codex: codex not found in PATH" >&2
  exit 127
fi
exec codex "$@"
